articles.title: Highly anticipated cholesterol drug fails to prevent heart attacks, strokes
articles.summary: An experimental drug that held great promise in driving down a dangerous form of cholesterol didn’t show any measurable impact on heart attack or stroke in a clinical trial.
articles.body: An experimental drug that held great promise in driving down a dangerous form of cholesterol didn’t show any measurable impact on heart attack or stroke in a clinical trial. The failure of the Novartis drug pelacarsen to help people who have high levels of lipoprotein(a) stunned researchers, who called it a massive blow to preventive cardiology. Results of the clinical trial of pelacarsen, an injection, presented Saturday at a meeting of the American Heart Association, found there were zero decreases in stroke, heart attack, cardiovascular deaths or the number of procedures to open blocked arteries or restore blood flow to the heart. “I really thought that this was going to be a slam dunk,” said Dr. Amanda Doran, an assistant professor of medicine in the division of cardiovascular medicine at Vanderbilt University Medical Center. Vanderbilt was one of nearly 800 sites involved in the clinical trial, called Horizon. “We were pretty invested, so it obviously hurts.” Pelacarsen targets a stealthy and particularly lethal form of cholesterol called lipoprotein(a), or Lp(a). Much like low-density lipoprotein — LDL, or the “bad” cholesterol — Lp(a) causes plaque to build up in arteries. But it also helps form blood clots, and unlike LDL, it is entirely genetic. About 1 in 5 Americans have high Lp(a), according to the American Heart Association. Most don’t realize they’re at risk. Because people are born with those high levels, diet and exercise have no effect. That’s why heart experts have been so keen to find a drug that would handle the problem. The Horizon trial included 8,322 people with high Lp(a) levels and who’d already had a heart attack, stroke or other heart problem within 10 years of starting the trial. The drug did reduce Lp(a) significantly, by 78%, compared to a placebo drug that cut levels by 13%. But that huge reduction ultimately meant nothing in terms of cardiovascular health. Dr. Steven Nissen, the chief academic officer of the Heart, Vascular & Thoracic Institute at the Cleveland Clinic, led the trial. He said the dismal results took him by “extreme surprise.” “Everybody, me included, believed that lowering levels of lipoprotein(a) substantially would reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events,” he said. “There is simply no evidence here that people that got more reduction did better.” The findings, also published Saturday in the New England Journal of Medicine, confounded Nissen and other cardiologists who’ve long known that controlling other markers of heart health — LDL and blood pressure, for example — provides clear benefits. “I have not seen a more shockingly neutral trial in a while,” said Dr. Karol Watson, co-director of the UCLA Program in Preventive Cardiology and a professor at UCLA’s David Geffen School of Medicine. Watson was not involved with the research. There are several theories as to why the drug didn’t work as anticipated. It’s possible, Watson said, that the therapy was given too late in life to make a difference. The average age of Horizon’s study participants was 60, and they were followed for an average of five years. “Remember that Lp(a) is a genetic disorder, so from the time a baby’s conceived, their Lp(a) is high. If we just swooped in in the last five years, maybe that’s too late,” Watson said. Study participants were also treated aggressively in other ways to drive down their LDL cholesterol and get blood pressure readings into a healthy range. Participants may have also been taking aspirin because of a history of heart attack or stroke, which could have lessened Lp(a)’s clotting risk. “How much of the Lp(a)-associated risk was remaining? We just don’t know,” Watson said. Does Lp(a) still matter as a marker of heart health? Doctors have only recently begun screening for it. Earlier this year, the American College of Cardiology and the American Heart Association released guidelines that every adult should have their Lp(a) levels measured. It’s a blood test that’s done once because levels are fixed and don’t change over time. Experts stress that Lp(a) remains an important and valuable indicator of heart disease risk, even though the Horizon study failed to show any health benefit to driving down Lp(a) levels. “None of that invalidates Lp(a) as a robust marker of cardiovascular disease risk,” said Dr. John Wilkins, a cardiologist at Northwestern Medicine and a professor in the division of cardiology at Northwestern University’s Feinberg School of Medicine. Wilkins was also one of the authors of the Lp(a) guidelines. “It’s still worth testing for Lp(a) because it can help identify individuals with a higher probability of an event, and we do have other interventions that can help reduce their risk,” Wilkins said. “It’s just that at present, at least with this particular drug in this particular group of patients, we did not see benefit. That doesn’t mean that we might not find something or some way to lower Lp(a) that reduces risk. We just need more science to figure that out.” UCLA’s Watson and Vanderbilt’s Doran agreed. “We have really good data to show that Lp(a) levels are predictive of disease,” Doran said. “People who have high Lp(a) need to be aware of that in order to pursue aggressive prevention strategies.” What’s next in treating Lp(a)? No further study of pelacarsen is planned, Nissen said, but similar drugs are in the pipeline: Eli Lilly’s lepodisiran, Amgen’s olpasiran and Silence Therapeutics’ zerlasiran. All are injections that work by blocking the liver’s ability to produce Lp(a), but use different approaches. Pelacarsen is what’s known as an antisense oligonucleotide. The others use a technology called small interfering RNA, or siRNA, and may have fewer side effects, such as injection site reactions, Nissen said, than pelacarsen. Like pelacarsen, all reduce Lp(a). Clinical trials to show whether they have any real-world heart health effects are ongoing. Eli Lilly is also studying an oral drug called muvalaplin, and CRISPR gene-editing technology designed to permanently switch off the gene that produces Lp(a) is in early development. “I’m still so hopeful,” Doran said. “We’re going to get it in the end.”

articles.title: Jack Campbell injury update ahead of Lions vs. Dolphins in Week 9
articles.summary: Detroit linebacker Jack Campbell's recovery from an on-field neck injury continues as the Lions prepare to face the Miami Dolphins in NFL Week 9.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell's road to recovery is on the hearts and minds of teammates, coaches and fans as the Lions prepare for their Week 9 road game against the Miami Dolphins .

Campbell and the Lions have provided progressively positive updates after the linebacker was carted off the field on Sunday, Nov. 1, when he fell limp to the Ford Field turf after tackling Minnesota Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson.

Campbell has been hospitalized at Henry Ford Hospital in Detroit since suffering an undisclosed spinal injury. While much remains publicly unknown about Campbell's diagnosis, recovery and long-term prognosis, here's what we know as the Lions (5-2) prepare for what's sure to be an emotional game against the 1-6 Dolphins .

What's the latest Jack Campbell injury update?

Campbell posted his first, and so far only, public statement following his injury on Wednesday, Nov. 4, announcing that he has full movement in his lower body and was continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body. It marked the first concrete update on the linebacker's condition since he suffered a neck injury during the Lions' Week 8 victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 1.

Prior to his statement, the updates had been more general and left many concerned about Campbell's condition after he was carted off the field on a backboard.

"I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic," Campbell wrote. "I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better."

Detroit Lions LB Jack Campbell suffers neck injury. See the emotional aftermath

The Lions have not provided updates about where Campbell is receiving treatment beyond saying that he was hospitalized following the injury, and Campbell on Wednesday, Nov. 4, thanking his caregivers at Henry Ford Hospital in Detroit and the Detroit Lions medical staff.

Campbell appears to have avoided the worst fears that immediately followed his injury, as his updates indicate that he has avoided full paralysis from the neck down. Campbell said he has "full movement in my lower body" and was working to regain upper-body movement as part of his recovery.

Does Jack Campbell have central cord syndrome?

Campbell's medical diagnosis has not yet been made public. Medical experts reached by USA TODAY did point out the uniqueness of Campbell's post-injury symptoms, saying that delayed recovery of upper-body movement could be associated with central cord syndrome. It's a rare medical condition common in people with spinal injuries who have fallen forward and land on their forehead and extend backward, similar to the action exhibited by Campbell's head and neck at impact.

"I think it's great news (if it's central cord syndrome) because it's an incomplete spinal-cord injury," neurosurgeon Dr. Betsy Grunch said, "and if he's already recovering as quickly as reported, then it's quite possible he can make a full recovery."

Is Jack Campbell out for the season? Will he play again?

The Lions have not provided any timeline for Campbell to return to football activities, as he likely faces an extended period of recovery and rest as he works toward regaining full function of his extremities.

Campbell, in his statement, said: "My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we'll get through this."

When do the Lions play the Dolphins in Week 9?

The Lions will play their first game without Campbell against the Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on Sunday, Nov. 8.

articles.title: Relationship expert explains why people ghost and what they may regret later
articles.summary: Relationship expert Monica Ricci shares why ghosting is a classic avoidance behavior and what it truly says about the person who disappears.
articles.body: If you've ever dated someone who stopped reaching out and responding to texts, without any conversation about ending the relationship, you’ve been ghosted. "Ghosting," or the sudden absence or unresponsiveness of a potential partner, is more than just feeling ignored by someone you’re interested in, according to Monica Ricci, a Georgia-based relationship coach — it's a complete disappearance without closure. Why do people ghost? Ricci suggested it’s a "classic avoidance behavior." "It's the same reason we procrastinate — we're avoiding some kind of discomfort," she said. THE MARRIAGE WARNING SIGN THAT MAY BE WORSE THAN FIGHTING — AND 4 WAYS TO TURN THINGS AROUND "It could be a fear of having a really hard conversation. It could be not wanting to disappoint a person," Ricci went on. "Someone could ghost because they just don't care enough. They're just not invested enough that they believe it [would] warrant communicating to say, ‘Hey, this isn't working for me.'" Those who do the ghosting may feel a sudden sense of relief, according to Ricci, but may also have lingering guilt around how the relationship was left unfinished. A new paper based on three studies, published in Sage Journals, suggests people who are ghosted underestimate the guilt and remorse felt by those who cut off contact. 5 MARRIAGE MISTAKES COUPLES MAKE WITHOUT REALIZING IT — AND HOW TO AVOID THEM "There's a part of you that may know that wasn't the best way to handle it," Ricci said. "And so it may stay with you a lot longer because it calls into question the kind of person you want to be." It’s easy to take ghosting personally, she noted. "But the truth is, if you're being ghosted, it says more about the person who ghosted you and their ability to have honest communication, their ability to step up in an uncomfortable situation and really choose their behavior over their discomfort." After a ghosting, the brain will automatically begin searching for patterns and answers to "make things make sense," Ricci said. WHY COUPLES SHOULD FLIRT WITH EACH OTHER EVERY DAY — PLUS THE ‘RED FLAG’ TO AVOID At some point, moving forward means accepting that you may never get an explanation and recognizing that being ghosted is not a reflection of your worth, according to the expert. "If a person can't have a conversation with you at the beginning of a relationship that is honest and frank, they probably weren't your person anyway," she added. How to communicate honestly Ricci, whose expertise is based on the Gottman Method — an approach to couples therapy focused on building emotional intimacy, improving communication and managing conflict — said seemingly difficult conversations can be easier than people expect. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "When you want to communicate that this dating relationship is not a good fit anymore, it's easiest to be very direct and brief," she said. This can be as simple as sending a text saying, "I have enjoyed getting to know you. I'm not feeling the kind of connection that I need to move forward, and I wish you all the best in finding a great match." "If a person can't have a conversation with you at the beginning of a relationship that is honest and frank, they probably weren't your person anyway." "You're honest, you're truthful, you're not making it about them being a bad person," she said. "You're saying, ‘I'm just not feeling the kind of connection I need to move forward.'" CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Although being forthright is the respectful option, it's not possible to control how the other person will feel or react, Ricci noted. "And this is sometimes where the ghosting comes from – we don't want to make someone feel bad," she said. "It’s this illusion that we have some control over how a person feels … But the reality is the least painful and kindest option is to just be direct." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ However, in a situation where you are being harassed, stalked or abused, ghosting may be the safest option, Ricci emphasized. "If someone is treating you really poorly, or harassing you, or stalking you … ghosting is absolutely the most appropriate," she said. "Cutting a person off completely, not responding, is the safest, smartest way to go."

articles.title: Son sounds alarm after father's medically assisted death in Canada: Way past appropriate'
articles.summary: Eric Edmeades says Canada's MAiD program moved so fast his father died before the family could prepare, warning safeguards have gone too far.
articles.body: A Canadian man's decision to end his life through the country's medically assisted dying program left his son stunned by how quickly the process unfolded, and now he's warning that the system has gone "way past appropriate." Eric Edmeades, founder of Speaker Nation, a training platform for speakers that teaches presentation skills and more, told Fox News Digital this week that his father Baz, who was in his late 70s and struggling with a combination of medical problems, began discussing Canada's Medical Assistance in Dying (MAiD) program after his health deteriorated in late 2023. But what Edmeades expected to be a months-long process suddenly accelerated, leaving the family with little time to prepare. I'M 25 WITH A TERMINAL DISEASE. WE NEED AN FDA COMMISSIONER THAT HEARS PEOPLE LIKE ME Edmeades said the family started taking the issue seriously in January, but at that stage, projections were that it would take at least six months. He and his wife traveled to Vancouver at the beginning of 2024 to visit his father. At that stage, it was still a speculative thing that was months away. "And then all of a sudden it was like, ‘No, it's next week,’" Edmeades recalled. His father died via MAiD on Feb. 27, 2024. He had been experiencing a sharp decline in his physical health and independence, particularly during the COVID-era lockdowns, according to his son. "He had been incredibly healthy most of his life," Edmeades said, describing a combination of symptoms that included epilepsy and neurological pain. Edmeades also questioned whether interactions between his father's medications could have contributed to his deteriorating condition. "When the lockdowns came along, and he could no longer go out and walk all the time, it really had a marked decrease in his physical ability and his sense of freedom and all that kind of stuff," he said. "And then there just came this point where life started sounding pointless to him," Edmeades said. CATHOLIC NUNS SUE NEW YORK, SAY ASSISTED SUICIDE LAW FORCES THEM TO VIOLATE THEIR FAITH Edmeades said his father had previously spoken about suicide, making his initial interest in medically assisted dying less surprising to the family. "Given that it wasn't the first time that he talked about suicide in his life, it wasn't particularly shocking, but he also wasn't talking about it in really alarmist terms. So, I wasn't overly worried about it," he said. Edmeades and his wife had already planned a trip to Vancouver and were able to spend time with his father before his death. "And one of the things I'm incredibly grateful for is that I had incidentally booked a trip out to Vancouver, and my wife and I got to spend time with him," Edmeades recalled. He thought he and and his wife would have another opportunity to visit. NEW YORK NUNS' CHALLENGE TO ASSISTED SUICIDE LAW IS ABOUT PROTECTING FREEDOM, LAWYER SAYS Edmeades said he was not in contact with his father's medical providers at the time and did not fully understand what had happened until afterward. "It happened so quickly that I only really started to piece together what happened when it was done," he said. Other family members and friends had also expressed concerns about his father's decision, according to Edmeades. He recalled that his brother openly opposed the decision and that one of his father's close friends spent approximately 45 minutes discussing the matter with him during his final days. "At that stage, you know, for him, the decision was made," Edmeades said. The experience has left Edmeades questioning whether Canada's assisted-dying program has adequate safeguards. He acknowledged that there may be circumstances in which medically assisted dying is appropriate but argued that Canada's implementation has gone too far. "What I see happening in Canada is way past appropriate," he said. Edmeades also raised concerns about the government's role in overseeing the system, arguing that decisions about eligibility should be insulated from political influence and potential financial incentives. "If I had to press a button and decide whether the MAiD program existed or didn't exist, I would say this," Edmeades said. "It should only ever exist if, and I mean if the process for approving people, it would be completely independent of government, and there could be no benefit to those people in making that preference in making that decision. Because otherwise there's a slippery slope, and we see that slippery slope." According to the Government of Canada, individuals seeking medical assistance in dying (MAiD) must be at least 18 years old, capable of making their own medical decisions, and eligible for publicly funded healthcare. They must also voluntarily request the procedure without outside pressure and provide informed consent. To qualify, applicants must have a serious, incurable illness, disease or disability, be experiencing an advanced and irreversible decline in their abilities, and face persistent physical or psychological suffering they consider intolerable and that cannot be relieved in a way they find acceptable. The government also announced legislation on Oct. 27, 2026, that would allow advance requests while preventing the planned expansion of MAiD eligibility to people whose sole underlying medical condition is mental illness. According to the BBC, Canada’s MAiD law, which legalized euthanasia in 2016, is responsible for one in every 20 deaths in Canada. NEW YORK NUNS WILL NOT BE FORCED TO COMPLY WITH ASSISTED-SUICIDE LAW WHILE CASE PROGRESSES A report from the Canadian Medical Association Journal covered by EWTN News claimed that implementing assisted suicide will "save" the Canadian healthcare system between $34.7 and $136.8 million per year. The study noted that patients and physicians should not consider costs when making such grave decisions. In a statement to Fox News Digital, Ian McLeod, senior advisor for media relations and Conseiller principal for the Department of Justice Canada, said, "Canadian law is extremely clear: medical assistance in dying (MAID) requires a voluntary request, freedom from external pressure, and the person’s informed consent, among other stringent eligibility criteria and safeguards. Knowingly failing to comply with these eligibility criteria and safeguards is a criminal offence." McLeod continued, "In the current MAID structure found in Canada’s Criminal Code, the mental illness exclusion is meant to exclude eligibility for MAID on the basis of a mental illness, including suicidal ideation. The proposed amendment to the mental illness exclusion in Bill C-41, the proposed Medical Assistance in Dying Safeguards Act, which was introduced on October 27, 2026, is meant to reinforce this." McLeod added, "This is why the Bill reinforces that, in situations where a person has a mental illness and an eligible medical condition (e.g. physical or neurodegenerative illness), eligibility must be determined on the basis of the qualifying medical condition. A mental illness may contribute to a person’s suffering, but it cannot be the basis for determining that the MAID eligibility criteria are met. Importantly, having a mental illness does not, in itself, make a person ineligible for MAID." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP McLeod said that patients whose natural deaths are not reasonably foreseeable must undergo eligibility assessments by two independent doctors or nurse practitioners, with at least 90 full days between the start of the first assessment and the assisted death. That waiting period, according to McLeod, can be shortened if both assessments are complete, both practitioners agree the patient is at imminent risk of losing the ability to consent, and the practitioner providing MAiD determines that a shorter period is appropriate. McLeod emphasized that federal requirements establish minimum safeguards, while provinces and territories oversee how MAiD is administered and may impose additional protections. He said questions about the program's oversight and delivery should therefore be directed to provincial or territorial authorities.

articles.title: Dinner dispute turns fatal; wife stabs ex-Army man to death in Ahmedabad
articles.summary: Ahmedabad Naroda: Woman allegedly stabs retired Army man husband to death after dinner dispute; accused Nirmala Kharadi arrested within hours, murder case filed.
articles.body: Ahmedabad: What began as a minor dinner-time argument in Naroda ended in tragedy when a 34-year-old woman allegedly plunged a kitchen knife into her husband’s chest during a heated dispute over the meal prepared at home. The victim, 39-year-old retired Army serviceman and GMDC contractual driver Dilipbhai Kharadi, succumbed to his injuries at a hospital, turning a domestic quarrel into a murder case.Police arrested the accused, identified as Nirmala Kharadi, and booked her for murder. The murder has left the couple’s two children without their father, while their mother remains in police custody.According to Naroda PI B M Katariya, Nirmala stabbed Dilip Kharadi on the left side of his chest after a heated argument at their residence in Naroda Smart City-2 around midnight on Thursday. “The couple had reportedly been quarrelling frequently over domestic and financial issues for nearly a year, and the latest dispute allegedly erupted over the dinner prepared that night,” he said.The PI said the accused will now be questioned to determine what led to the fatal quarrel. According to police, the couple had been facing minor domestic disputes for some time. On Thursday, an argument escalated when the wife allegedly responded angrily, leading to a heated exchange in which both parties abused each other. The confrontation eventually culminated in the stabbing, police said.According to the complaint filed by Dilip’s father, 73-year-old Somaji Kharadi, a retired unarmed ASI of Rajkot city police, the couple often argued over household matters, including what food should be cooked. On Thursday night, another disagreement broke out, during which Nirmala allegedly lost her temper, picked up a kitchen knife and attacked her husband.The murder came to light after Nirmala allegedly called her brother-in-law, Mukesh, around midnight and informed him that she had stabbed Dilip in the chest during an argument. She allegedly told him that her husband had become unconscious and that she was taking him to Shalby Hospital.On Friday afternoon, Mukesh informed his father that Dilip had been injured in a quarrel and admitted to hospital. Somaji, accompanied by family members, rushed to the hospital but was informed by doctors that his son had succumbed to his injuries.The complainant stated that he noticed a stab wound on the left side of Dilip’s chest, along with injuries on his right cheek, right upper arm, and near the thumbs of both hands. He also said the family had initially withheld news of the death from him to spare him the shock. Dilip retired from the Army in 2022.Naroda police formed multiple teams and analysed CCTV footage while gathering local intelligence to trace the accused. Nirmala was arrested within hours of the crime. Police registered a case of murder along with offences under the Gujarat Police Act and are continuing their investigation.The PI said that the dispute erupted after the husband asked why she had cooked a particular vegetable and this was countered by the wife, which eventually ended up with both the husband and wife abusing each other. articles.title: Pro-trans activists hold rally against Washington state ballot initiative to protect girls sports
articles.summary: Protesters marched through Seattle Thursday after Washington voters approved Initiative 638 barring biological males from girls' K-12 sports.
articles.body: Transgender-rights supporters marched through downtown Seattle Thursday after Washington voters approved a measure barring biological males from girls’ K–12 interscholastic sports, setting up a potential court battle over the new restrictions. Demonstrators gathered at Westlake Park before marching toward Pike Place Market, according to KUOW. The protest followed the passage of Initiative 638, which also requires students seeking to compete in girls’ sports to provide medical verification of their biological sex. The measure had 56.8% support in returns reported Thursday by FOX 13 Seattle. The Associated Press called its passage Wednesday evening, with ballots still being counted. WASHINGTON STATE VOTERS APPEAR TO PASS FIRST-EVER BALLOT MEASURE SEPARATING BOYS AND GIRLS SPORTS "I was kind of expecting it, but it was still devastating nonetheless," Evan Gortner of Gender Equity Movement, which organized the protest, told KUOW. Marchers chanted, "638 is trans hate." Some attendees also criticized Democratic leaders for not doing more to defeat the initiative. The result delivered a victory to Let’s Go Washington, the conservative group behind the measure, even as voters rejected two other initiatives it backed concerning parental rights and the repeal of the state’s tax on high earners. Supporters argue that separating girls’ sports by biological sex protects fairness, safety and athletic opportunities for female students. Opponents contend the restrictions discriminate against transgender students and could subject girls to intrusive medical verification. WOMEN WHO FACED BIOLOGICAL MALES IN GIRLS' SPORTS AND LOCKER ROOMS SPEAK OUT AHEAD OF WASHINGTON STATE VOTE The dispute now extends beyond the election results. Gender Justice League Executive Director Danni Askini told KUOW her organization was consulting partners and evaluating a possible challenge on student-privacy grounds. The group had not formally announced a lawsuit in that Nov. 5 report. The ACLU of Washington also condemned the outcome, but told KUOW it does not discuss potential litigation. That response did not announce a lawsuit. Washington Democrats, meanwhile, have said they support other organizations pursuing challenges but will not bring a case themselves. "WA Dems will not be challenging the initiative in court. We believe there will be organizations who do and we support those efforts," the party previously told OutKick. Party Chair Shasti Conrad called the initiative unconstitutional in a Nov. 5 statement. The measure’s medical-verification requirement has become a central point of contention. Its text requires a health examination and consent form, or another statement signed by a student’s personal healthcare provider, verifying biological sex as part of the required routine sports physical. That verification must rely on reproductive anatomy, genetic makeup or naturally produced testosterone levels. The text does not prescribe a particular examination or test. Washington has allowed students to compete on teams consistent with their gender identity since 2007. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The debate also prompted protests from female athletes before the election. About a dozen Camas girls declined to race against a transgender teammate on Oct. 13, OutKick previously reported. For schools, the immediate question is how to carry out the new requirements. The Washington Interscholastic Activities Association told KUOW it was preparing changes for Dec. 3 and reviewing implementation, including physical-examination requirements. It said updated guidance and forms would go to schools after legal review.

articles.title: Certain sleep habits could offer clues to hidden type of depression, scientists say
articles.summary: A study of over 11,000 Australian adults links specific sleep habits and circadian rhythm disruptions to a newly proposed subtype of depression.
articles.body: A person's sleep habits may help identify a newly proposed subtype of depression linked to the body's internal clock. In a study of 11,380 Australian adults with a history of depression, about 23% met researchers' criteria for what they called "circadian depression." The profile included at least three of six features: being an evening person, waking up feeling very tired, sleeping longer during the worst periods of depression, experiencing seasonal changes, having a later midpoint between falling asleep and waking up, and experiencing "social jetlag," a large shift in sleep timing between workdays and days off. The seasonal changes could involve sleep, mood, activity, appetite, weight or energy. THE DAYTIME HABIT THAT COULD TRANSFORM YOUR SLEEP, ACCORDING TO NEW STUDY The study, published on Oct. 20 in The British Journal of Psychiatry, could eventually help guide more personalized care for patients with depression, according to the researchers. "Depression is not a uniform illness, and understanding the characteristics of different subtypes means we can give people earlier access to treatments that will be most effective for them," first author Emiliana Tonini, Ph.D., from the University of Sydney's Brain and Mind Centre, said in a statement. The label, however, is not a formal diagnosis and needs independent replication and further study, the researchers noted. Treatment questions People in the circadian group reported an earlier onset of depression and more severe symptoms than those who did not meet the criteria. They were also more likely to report weight gain during depressive episodes. They also reported poorer responses and more side effects with two common classes of antidepressants, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs). POPULAR SLEEP AIDS BEFORE SURGERY COULD PREVENT PAINKILLER DEPENDENCE LATER Participants reported how well their medications worked, but the study did not explain why some were less effective and did not test treatments aimed at adjusting the body’s internal clock. Researchers said light exposure, regular sleep schedules and melatonin-related approaches warrant further study. Dr. Ian Hickie, a study co-author and professor of psychiatry at the University of Sydney, said the proposed profile "cuts across existing historic subtypes" of depression, most commonly atypical and bipolar depression, because they share features such as low energy and oversleeping. COMMON GYM SUPPLEMENT COULD HELP FIGHT DEPRESSION, NEW RESEARCH SUGGESTS Atypical depression can also involve weight gain, while bipolar depression refers to depressive episodes in people with bipolar disorder, which also involves periods of unusually elevated or irritable mood and increased energy. "We define circadian only by sleep-wake and circadian features," Hickie told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES For some people with this profile, Hickie said sleep-wake disruption may be more than a symptom of depression. "This type of circadian disturbance is not simply a consequence, but the underlying cause," he wrote. The study itself, however, could not establish whether body-clock disruption caused depression or resulted from it. Staying up late or having trouble waking does not necessarily indicate depression. Participants had already reported depression, which in some cases was severe, recurring or long-lasting. Participants in the circadian group also reported more manic-like experiences. John Puls, a psychotherapist and adjunct professor at Florida Atlantic University, said those symptoms could help explain their reported response to antidepressants. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "SSRIs are not meant to treat these more significant mental health symptoms that go far beyond depressive symptoms," Puls, who was not involved in the study, told Fox News Digital. "In fact, some SSRIs can actually worsen manic symptoms, which lead to poor sleep." Study limitations There were several limitations to the study, the researchers acknowledged. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Participants reported their own sleep patterns and treatment experiences, and the cross-sectional analysis didn't show whether sleep disruption preceded or followed depressive symptoms. All participants were of European ancestry, so the findings may not apply to other populations. Jillian Amodio, a Maryland-based psychotherapist and founder of Moms For Mental Health, cautioned against using the findings as "a benchmark for treating each person in the same way." "Biological, environmental, social and psychological factors all need to be accounted for," Amodio, who was not involved in the research, told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Researchers should examine more populations, including people who work night shifts, and account for differences in time zones and seasons, according to Amodio. The study was led by researchers at the University of Sydney and QIMR Berghofer Medical Research Institute, with co-authors from institutions in Australia, the U.K. and the U.S.

articles.title: Swansea mum tries to raise £2.95m for son's dementia treatment
articles.summary: The dementia treatment for children is available in the US, with funding for UK children unclear.
articles.body:
The mum of a five-year-old boy with a rare form of dementia has to pay almost £3m for his life saving treatment.

Tate McDaid, from Swansea, was diagnosed with Sanfilippo Syndrome - a form of dementia that just over 100 UK children have - when he was four .

In September, the first gene therapy to treat the condition in children was approved in the US.

His mum Tammy said she spent "months praying" for its approval but discovered the treatment is to set cost £2.95 million per child, with it unclear how families outside the US can fund this.

Health officials from Wales are currently talking to those in the US to see what potential access pathways there are for Tate.

"I was excited when the treatment initially got approved but then reality hit hard the next day," Tammy said.

This was when she read the US price for the one-time treatment had been set at $3.95 million.

Tammy contacted Ultragenyx, who developed the treatment, in the hope of understanding how families outside the US, who do not have health insurance there, will cover the costs.

"We understand what they are charging for American citizens, but they've got health insurance," she added.

"Not even just the UK, but everyone else in the world looking for this treatment."

Explaining how the US approved drug, FAYUVI, would work for families outside the US, Ultragenyx said: "There is not a single estimate we can provide for the total cost of care for an international patient, as those costs would depend on the patient's individual medical needs and the treating institution."

The Society for Mucopolysaccharide Diseases , a charity which helps children living with Sanfilippo Syndrome, said about 140 children in the UK have the condition.

There is currently no cure for Sanfilippo Syndrome Type A, also called Mucopolysaccharidosis type III (MPS III), but the new drug could delay its onset, and allow Tate to remain active for longer.

The condition, described as "childhood Alzheimer's" or "childhood dementia" due to its neurodegenerative nature, causes the gradual loss of abilities, such as walking and eating.

It can progress more rapidly after the age of five, which is why Tammy said "it's really a battle of time" for her to raise enough money to get her son the treatment that is not available yet in the UK.

She said: "If a millionaire turned around tomorrow and gave us the money, we'd go to the US straight away."

With Tate turning six this month, Tammy doesn't believe time is on their side.

"Tate is already shown signs of cognitive decline," she added.

"The older he gets the less the treatment will work and the more ability he will lose in the process.

"I feel like we are at a turning point and I'm petrified."

Describing him as "the happiest little man" who is "blissfully unaware" of his problems, Tammy explained how important Tate's mobility is to him.

"He doesn't speak, he's never spoken. But his mobility is everything to him and that is why I'm fighting for it," she said.

Tammy began raising money before the new drug was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration and now has more than £160,000.

But this covers only about 5% of the total estimated cost of the treatment.

"Unfortunately, we're in a world where we need millions, not hundreds of thousands," she added.

"I'm just really hoping by some miracle the pharmaceutical company eventually come back to us and say they can do it for a little bit cheaper, but it's still going to be in the millions."

Ultragenyx said: "We are pursuing a global regulatory strategy, and FDA approval is an important first step in our long-term goal of bringing this treatment option to families around the world.

"We also understand the urgency families affected by Sanfilippo syndrome Type A face in identifying treatment options and why some may consider travelling to the US to access gene therapy.

"We recommend families work with their child's healthcare provider to understand what potential access pathways may exist before assuming this is their only option."

Staff from the Noah's Ark Children's Hospital in Cardiff are currently discussing this with officials in the US on the family's behalf.

articles.title: Simple bedtime change may help some individuals lose weight, study finds
articles.summary: An NYU clinical trial found that moving bedtime just one hour earlier led to weight loss in prediabetes patients, even without longer sleep.
articles.body: Falling asleep earlier was linked to greater weight loss in adults with prediabetes, according to new research. An analysis of data from a randomized trial led by the NYU Rory Meyers College of Nursing found that each hour earlier participants fell asleep was associated with roughly 1. 3 pounds of weight loss over eight weeks, although the finding does not prove that moving bedtime earlier causes weight loss. "When we fall asleep — not just how much we sleep — seems to be an important and overlooked factor for weight loss and metabolic health," Susan Kohl Malone, an assistant professor at the nursing college and the study's lead author, said in a press release. POPULAR WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS MAY PREVENT PREDIABETES FROM TURNING INTO DIABETES The investigation, published in the journal Nursing Research, evaluated 196 adults diagnosed with prediabetes who routinely logged fewer than 6.5 hours of sleep nightly. Half the group took part in an eight-week lifestyle education course on diet, exercise and stress. The other half received the same training alongside behavioral coaching meant to get them to go to bed earlier in gradual phases. DIETITIAN REVEALS SIMPLE EATING STRATEGY FOR BETTER SLEEP — AND ONE HABIT TO AVOID Researchers tracked participants’ blood sugar, sleep and activity using sensors, sleep logs and wrist-worn monitors. Neither group showed significant improvements in blood sugar. Both groups lost weight, but those receiving sleep coaching did not lose significantly more than those receiving lifestyle education alone. "While we expected that extending sleep would improve glucose levels and weight loss in adults with prediabetes who sleep for shorter periods, this wasn't the case in our study," Malone said. Participants who received sleep coaching did report better sleep quality and less daytime drowsiness, and they gradually began going to bed earlier. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER In a separate analysis across both groups, participants who shifted their sleep earlier tended to lose more weight. The researchers suggested the body’s internal clock may help explain the findings. Staying up late can increase exposure to artificial light, which may activate the body’s stress response and affect hormones that regulate hunger. Remaining awake late also coincides with the hours when human insulin sensitivity is at its lowest. "In contrast, falling asleep earlier may limit late-night eating and better align food intake with the body's optimal metabolic window," Malone noted. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES The trial ran for only eight weeks, which means it's unclear whether participants could maintain earlier bedtimes or sustain weight loss over the long term. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ While participants wore wrist monitors, key sleep metrics like rest quality and daytime drowsiness relied heavily on self-reported logs. The findings also show an association across the study group rather than proven cause and effect. Participants receiving sleep coaching fell asleep about 12 minutes earlier on average, according to Malone, which produced no measurable improvement in blood sugar levels. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The study received funding from the National Institute of Nursing Research, a division of the National Institutes of Health, and was conducted in collaboration with researchers from the University of Delaware.

articles.title: 'Embarcou bem', diz pai de adolescente que passou mal e morreu em voo | G1
articles.standfirst: Diogo Pompermayer Marchiori, de 13 anos, sofreu parada cardíaca a caminho de avaliação médica na capital paulista. Ramon Marchiori relembrou perfil amoroso do filho e denunciou falhas em equipamentos e logística no aeroporto.
articles.summary: Diogo Pompermayer, de 13 anos, sofreu parada cardíaca a caminho de SP. Ramon Marchiori relembrou perfil amoroso do filho e denunciou falhas em equipamentos de socorro.
articles.body:
Ramon Marchiori (à esquerda) falou sobre a morte do filho, Diogo Pompermayer Marchiori (à direita), de 13 anos, em voo entre o Espírito Santo e São Paulo. — Foto: Acervo de família

Amoroso e brincalhão: foi assim que o empresário Ramon Marchiori, de 48 anos, definiu o filho Diogo Pompermayer Marchiori. O adolescente morreu na quinta-feira (5), após sofrer uma parada cardíaca em voo que saiu do Aeroporto de Vitória, no Espírito Santo, com destino a Guarulhos, em São Paulo.

Em entrevista exclusiva ao g1 , Ramon disse que o filho era muito ligado à família. Aos 13 anos, tinha uma rotina que incluía a escola, as brincadeiras com o irmão mais novo, de 4 anos, e as viagens ao lado dos pais.

A relação com os familiares era uma das características mais lembradas pelo pai. Diogo era carinhoso com os pais e com o irmão caçula, com quem costumava brincar. Na escola, também era querido pelos colegas. “Era um menino muito agradável. Difícil mesmo era falar um palavrão”, contou.

Torcedor do Botafogo, também compartilhava com o pai a paixão pelo futebol, contou o empresário. A paixão pelo Botafogo rendeu uma das lembranças mais especiais entre pai e filho. Os dois viajaram de ônibus até a Argentina, em 2024, para acompanhar a final da Libertadores, quando o time enfrentava o Atlético Mineiro e saiu campeão.

“Foram três dias de estrada na ida e outros três na volta. A experiência ficou marcada na minha memória. Foi a maior alegria da minha vida e da dele também”, recordou.

O problema cardíaco era acompanhado desde os primeiros meses de vida. Segundo o pai, pouco depois de receber alta da maternidade, Diogo apresentou alterações na respiração e nos batimentos cardíacos. A família o levou para atendimento em Cachoeiro de Itapemirim, na Região Sul do estado, onde ele ficou internado por 20 dias na Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI). Durante a internação, os exames identificaram uma infecção por bactéria hospitalar.

Depois da alta, Diogo passou a fazer acompanhamento médico no município. Ao longo dos anos, manteve o tratamento e utilizava medicamentos, mas, segundo o pai, levava uma vida ativa: frequentava a escola, brincava e viajava — e já havia pegado voos para a Inglaterra, Belo Horizonte e São Paulo.

A viagem para o estado paulista, na quinta-feira (5), também tinha relação com o tratamento de Diogo. Por indicação da médica que o acompanhava em Cachoeiro, a família procurou um especialista no Hospital Albert Einstein, na capital paulista, para dar continuidade ao acompanhamento e avaliar possíveis mudanças na medicação. Segundo o pai, a consulta já estava sendo planejada havia mais de dois anos.

Diogo Pompermayer Marchiori morreu durante um voo do Espírito Santo para São Paulo — Foto: Acervo pessoal

Sintomas no ar e equipamentos com defeito

Segundo Ramon, o filho embarcou na quinta-feira (5) se sentindo bem. “Nós fizemos muitas viagens em família. Fomos para Belo Horizonte e até mesmo para fora do país, na Inglaterra. E o Diogo nunca se sentiu mal”, contou o empresário.

O empresário disse que, após o serviço de bordo, o filho comeu um biscoito, dormiu por um período e, ao acordar, disse à mãe que sentia uma dor muito forte no peito. Em seguida, ficou desacordado.

“Depois disso, eu e minha esposa começamos a gritar, pedindo ajuda. As aeromoças nos levaram para os fundos do avião para iniciar os primeiros socorros, junto com outras duas enfermeiras que estavam no voo”, disse.

Segundo Ramon, os tripulantes trouxeram dois cilindros de oxigênio, mas nenhum deles continha oxigênio. Ele também afirmou que o desfibrilador estava funcionando, mas tinha apenas 4% de bateria.

“Os tripulantes trouxeram dois cilindros de oxigênio. Os dois não tinham ar, não tinham oxigênio dentro. E o desfibrilador, que estava funcionando, só tinha 4% de bateria”, afirmou.

Demora da ambulância e falta das escadas

O pai do adolescente contou ainda que, quando o avião pousou em Guarulhos, não havia nenhuma ambulância na pista do aeroporto, apesar de o piloto ter solicitado o serviço. Segundo ele, quando a ambulância chegou, a equipe ainda precisou aguardar a disponibilização das escadas, que estavam a cerca de 15 metros da aeronave, mas não haviam sido conectadas ao avião.

O empresário disse ao g1 que chegou a ameaçar pular da aeronave para agilizar o atendimento.

“Eu comecei a gritar que ia pular da aeronave, e minha esposa falou para que eu pulasse e fosse buscar a escada”, contou.

Ramon contou que, após a ameaça, um grupo de agentes que atuava na pista levou as escadas até a aeronave. Em seguida, Diogo foi transportado para a ambulância. De acordo com o empresário, o trajeto até o hospital durou menos de sete minutos. Ele afirmou, no entanto, que a ambulância contava apenas com um socorrista e uma enfermeira.

“Quando chegamos ao hospital, o Diogo já estava sem vida. Os médicos ainda tentaram reanimá-lo com o desfibrilador, mas, infelizmente, ele não resistiu”, relatou.

Um passageiro, que não quis se identificar, gravou um vídeo durante o socorro, quando o avião já havia pousado. Na gravação, ele denunciou uma suposta demora no atendimento dos socorristas. “Olha a lentidão do pessoal da ambulância”, disse ele na gravação.

O pai do adolescente disse ao g1 que representantes da Gol foram até o hospital e prestaram apoio à família. Segundo ele, a companhia aérea também custeou o traslado do corpo para o Espírito Santo.

Questionada sobre as falhas nos equipamentos, a Gol informou que "todos os protocolos para este tipo de situação foram seguidos e o passageiro foi encaminhado em ambulância para hospital em Guarulhos".

A concessionária GRU Airport afirmou que "a equipe de resposta a emergência da GRU Airport foi acionada e, seguindo os protocolos de segurança, prestou os primeiros socorros e encaminhou o passageiro ao hospital mais próximo".

articles.title: Menina de 12 anos morre após ser arrastada por correnteza de riacho | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima estava em um grupo de crianças e adolescentes em Rolândia. Bombeiros chegaram a receber informações sobre outros desaparecidos, mas foram avisados de que todos os demais voltaram para casa.
articles.summary: Vítima estava em um grupo de crianças e adolescentes em Rolândia.
articles.body:
Kawane Aparecida Proença, de 12 anos, morreu após ser arrastada por correnteza. — Foto: Foto: Cobra News | Redes Sociais

Kawane Aparecida Proença, de 12 anos, morreu após ser arrastada pela correnteza de um riacho após uma cabeça d'água em Rolândia , no norte do Paraná, neste sábado (7). A prefeitura do município e o colégio estadual onde a criança estudava se manifestaram com notas de pesar, neste domingo (8), afirmando que se trata de uma 'perda irreparável'. Veja abaixo na íntegra.

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, a menina estava com um grupo de crianças e adolescentes, em um total de oito pessoas, que foi surpreendido pelo aumento repentino do nível da água.

🔎 A cabeça d'água é um fenômeno caracterizado pelo aumento repentino do volume e da força da correnteza de rios e riachos, geralmente provocado por chuvas intensas em regiões próximas às nascentes ou em outros pontos da bacia hidrográfica.

Os bombeiros foram acionados após duas crianças procurarem ajuda em uma residência próxima ao riacho. Elas relataram que três pessoas haviam sido levadas pela correnteza.

Bombeiros encontraram corpo da menina em riacho — Foto: Cobra News

Durante as buscas, os socorristas encontraram a menina de 12 anos em parada cardiorrespiratória e iniciaram as manobras de reanimação. No entanto, ela não resistiu. A morte foi confirmada ainda no sábado. O corpo da criança foi encaminhado para o Instituto Médico Legal de Londrina, onde deu entrada por volta das 21h10.

As equipes continuaram as buscas com base nos relatos de que outras duas pessoas também haviam desaparecido, mas receberam a confirmação de que elas conseguiram sair da água e que já estavam em casa.

Prefeitura de Rolândia e colégio se manifestaram sobre morte de criança

A Prefeitura de Rolândia se manifestou, neste domingo (8), através de uma nota de pesar, confirmando a identidade de vítima. No texto, a gestão municipal afirmou que a morte de Kawane Aparecida Proença foi uma 'perda irreparável'. Veja na íntegra:

"É com profunda tristeza e pesar que a Prefeitura de Rolândia lamenta o falecimento de Kawane Aparecida Proença, de 12 anos, nascida em 10 de junho de 2014, aluna do Colégio Estadual Professor José Alexandre Chiarelli, que vítima de um afogamento ocorrido no Monte Carlo, no final da tarde deste sábado (07/11).

A partida tão precoce de Kawane representa uma perda irreparável e deixa um profundo sentimento de dor e tristeza entre familiares, amigos, colegas, professores e toda a comunidade escolar.

Uma tragédia que comove toda a nossa cidade e nos une em solidariedade à família, diante de uma despedida tão dolorosa.

Neste momento de imensa tristeza, a Prefeitura de Rolândia manifesta suas mais sinceras condolências aos familiares e amigos, desejando força, fé e conforto para enfrentar essa perda.

Que Deus, em sua infinita misericórdia, acolha Kawane e conceda consolo e amparo a todos os corações que hoje choram sua partida".

Prefeitura de Rolândia postou mensagem de pesar. — Foto: Foto: Redes Sociais

O Colégio Cívico Militar Professor José Alexandre Chiarelli, onde a menina estudava, também se manifestou em nota publicada nas redes sociais. Veja:

"É com profundo pesar, dor e imensa tristeza que a comunidade escolar do Colégio Estadual CM Prof José Alexandre Chiarelli recebe a notícia do falecimento da nossa querida aluna Kawane Aparecida Proença.

​Neste momento de luto e dor imensurável, professores, funcionários, colegas de turma e toda a comunidade escolar se unem em oração e solidariedade à família, parentes e amigos. A partida precoce da Kawane deixa uma lacuna imensa em nossos corações e em nossos corredores, onde sua alegria e presença deixarão saudades eternas.

​Que Deus possa confortar o coração de todos os familiares e amigos, dando forças para superar esta perda irreparável. ​Descanse em paz, querida Kawane".

articles.title: Adolescente atingida por árvore em Santa Bárbara passa por cirurgia | G1
articles.standfirst: Jovem de 14 anos estava no Parque dos Ipês, em Santa Bárbara d'Oeste, quando temporal começou repentinamente. Cirurgias foram realizadas com sucesso.
articles.summary: Após ser atingida por uma árvore no Parque dos Ipês, em Santa Bárbara d'Oeste, adolescente de 14 anos passa por cirurgias bem-sucedidas e evita amputação.
articles.body:
A adolescente de 14 anos, atingida por uma árvore durante um temporal , passou por uma cirurgia de alto risco na cabeça após sofrer um traumatismo em Santa Bárbara d'Oeste (SP). Ela também precisou ter um dos pés reconstruídos por conta das lesões causadas pelo acidente.

As informações foram passadas por uma prima da jovem, Carolina Bianca. Segundo Bianca, os procedimentos cirúrgicos foram realizados com sucesso no sábado (7).

Com isso, os médicos descartaram a amputação dos dedos do pé. A jovem segue em acompanhamento pós-operatório até a última atualização desta reportagem, segundo Bianca.

Segundo a prima, a adolescente estava no parque com familiares e amigos, organizando os últimos detalhes de um chá de bebê que será realizado no local. Quando o tempo começou a mudar e indicou a chegada da chuva, o grupo decidiu deixar o espaço.

Árvores caídas no Parque dos Ipês, em Santa Bárbara d'Oeste, onde uma jovem de 14 anos estava quando foi atingida — Foto: Júnia Vasconcelos

Próximo à área dos brinquedos infantis, o vendaval ficou mais forte e derrubou galhos. O grupo tentou se proteger, mas uma árvore caiu e atingiu a adolescente.

"Uma árvore caiu bem na minha frente e atingiu ela, e eu não vi pois o vento estava muito forte e tinha terra e galhos acertando a gente", relatou a prima.

A prima ainda conta que logo depois, outras árvores começaram a cair. "Eu e meu esposo tentávamos encontrar uma maneira de sair daquele local. Tentávamos voltar, caía uma árvore, tentávamos avançar, caía outra", disse.

"Não sabíamos para onde ir nem o que fazer. O que me lembro é que foram pelo menos três árvores caindo", completou.

Ela, o marido e amigos que estavam no local conseguiram retirar a jovem debaixo da árvore e levá-la ao pronto-socorro.

A Prefeitura de Santa Bárbara d'Oeste informou que a adolescente deu entrada em estado grave no Pronto-Socorro Dr. Edison Mano.

Após ser estabilizada, ela foi transferida pela equipe da Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI) móvel do município para o Hospital Estadual de Sumaré devido à gravidade dos ferimentos.

articles.title: Motorista morre e carro fica destruído após batida em poste em SC | G1
articles.standfirst: Passageira sobreviveu e foi levada ao hospital. Acidente ocorreu na manhã deste domingo (8) em São Joaquim.
articles.summary: Passageira sobreviveu e foi levada ao hospital.
articles.body:
Um motorista morreu e o carro ficou destruído após uma batida em poste na manhã deste domingo (8) em São Joaquim , na Serra de Santa Catarina . A passageira sobreviveu e foi levada ao hospital, informou a Polícia Militar Rodoviária (PMRv).

O Corpo de Bombeiros Militar foi chamado perto das 6h à SC-114, também conhecida como Avenida Ivo Silveira. No local, os socorristas viram o carro, um Voyage branco, já batido no poste, fora da pista.

Havia duas pessoas dentro do veículo. O motorista, de 25 anos, natural de Lages , na mesma região, já estava sem sinais vitais.

O corpo dele estava preso às ferragens e os bombeiros fizeram uma operação com equipamentos hidráulicos para fazer o resgate. Ele foi deixado aos cuidados da Polícia Científica.

Carro fica destruído após batida em poste em São Joaquim, SC — Foto: CBMSC/Divulgação

Já a passageira, de 31 anos, estava consciente, mas confusa. Ela tinha ferimentos no rosto, dores nas costelas e lesões nos braços e pernas.

Ela recebeu os primeiros socorros do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (SAMU). Depois, foi levada ao Hospital de Caridade Coração de Jesus, em São Joaquim.

Cena do acidente indica que motorista perdeu controle do carro

A PMRv informou que a batida ocorreu no km 304 e que o carro tinha placas de São Joaquim.

Conforme a polícia, elementos técnicos, como posição final e danos do veículo, além das marcas na via, indicam que o motorista provavelmente perdeu o controle do automóvel.

Ele seguia no sentido Sul da SC-114 quando saiu da pista e bateu no poste.

articles.title: Jovem passa 35 dias com dois corações em cirurgia inédita no Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Diagnosticado com insuficiência cardíaca grave e hipertensão pulmonar severa, Marcelo passou por procedimento criado por médico brasileiro. Técnica permite que dois corações funcionem juntos.
articles.summary: Diagnosticado com insuficiência cardíaca grave e hipertensão pulmonar severa, Marcelo passou por procedimento criado por médico brasileiro. Técnica permite que dois corações funcionem juntos.
articles.body:
Um jovem diagnosticado com insuficiência cardíaca grave e hipertensão pulmonar severa passou 35 dias com dois corações após ser submetido a uma técnica de transplante desenvolvida pelo cirurgião brasileiro Fábio Gaiotto. O procedimento foi realizado no Einstein Hospital Israelita, em São Paulo, e é o segundo caso de aplicação da técnica no mundo.

Marcelo, estudante de história, recebeu o diagnóstico há três anos, quando tinha apenas 17 anos. Na época, a gravidade do quadro indicava a necessidade de um transplante de coração e pulmão.

A possibilidade de realizar um procedimento diferente surgiu com a técnica desenvolvida por Gaiotto, que permite tratar a hipertensão pulmonar e substituir o coração doente sem a necessidade de transplantar também os pulmões.

Na técnica, o coração de um doador é conectado ao coração do paciente, permitindo que os dois funcionem simultaneamente.

Com o passar do tempo, a pressão pulmonar diminui. Quando os pulmões apresentam melhora, o coração doente é retirado, permanecendo apenas o órgão transplantado.

Técnica usa coração de um doador conectado ao coração do paciente. — Foto: Reprodução / Fantástico

Segundo o cirurgião Fábio Gaiotto, a técnica utiliza uma conexão diferente entre os órgãos para permitir a recuperação dos pulmões.

O primeiro procedimento foi realizado em 2021, no urbanista Lincoln, que tinha 54 anos na época. Ele passou 45 dias com dois corações e, segundo a reportagem, está plenamente recuperado.

Em março de 2026, Marcelo chegou de helicóptero ao Einstein Hospital Israelita, em São Paulo, e foi encaminhado imediatamente para a cirurgia.

O jovem permaneceu 35 dias com os dois corações. Durante esse período, o coração transplantado sofreu duas paradas, e Marcelo precisou ser entubado.

Após acordar, enfrentou uma longa recuperação devido à perda muscular. O processo incluiu sessões de fisioterapia para recuperar os movimentos, a capacidade de ficar em pé e a autonomia para realizar atividades cotidianas.

Ao longo da internação, Marcelo voltou a caminhar com auxílio, tocar piano, dançar e realizar tarefas simples, como fazer a própria barba.

O tratamento foi realizado por meio do Programa de Apoio ao Desenvolvimento Institucional do Sistema Único de Saúde (Proadi-SUS), que permite a utilização da estrutura e da tecnologia do Einstein no atendimento a pacientes do SUS.

Fantástico promove o encontro dos dois únicos pacientes que passaram pela técnica que usa dois corações simultâneos. — Foto: Reprodução / Fantástico

O Fantástico acompanhou um encontro entre Marcelo e Lincoln, os dois pacientes submetidos à técnica desenvolvida por Gaiotto.

Durante a conversa, Marcelo contou que a experiência de Lincoln foi fundamental para que aceitasse passar pela cirurgia.

"Eu queria dizer pra você que você foi um boost, assim, você foi a força motriz pra eu conseguir aceitar o transplante, aceitar fazer esse método novo, né?", disse Marcelo.

Lincoln também destacou a experiência compartilhada pelos dois.

"Eu acho que só tem duas pessoas no mundo que podem entender. Só eu e você, né?", afirmou.

O cirurgião Fábio Gaiotto participou do encontro e ressaltou o trabalho conjunto de médicos, fisioterapeutas, enfermeiros e outros profissionais envolvidos nos procedimentos.

Marcelo World passou 35 dias com dois corações. — Foto: Reprodução / Fantástico

Apesar dos resultados positivos nos dois primeiros pacientes, a técnica ainda está em fase de avaliação científica.

O médico Fábio Gaiotto pretende realizar o procedimento em mais quatro pacientes para reunir dados e validar o método desenvolvido. Segundo o cirurgião, a continuidade da técnica dependerá dos resultados obtidos ao longo dos seis casos previstos no protocolo.

articles.title: Chuva no Rio: mulher morre em desabamento e ventos chegam a 60 km/h | G1
articles.standfirst: No sábado (7), por conta do temporal, 1 mulher morreu na Zona Oeste do Rio. Neste domingo, na Marambaia registrou vento de 59,4 km/h. Sistema Alerta Rio também identificou chuva em bairros das zonas Central, Norte e Oeste.
articles.summary: Chuva no Rio de Janeiro causa morte em desabamento e mobiliza bombeiros em 140 ocorrências; ventos atingiram 60 km/h e previsão indica mais temporal para este domingo.
articles.body:
Cristo Redentor visto do Flamengo encoberto pelas nuvens — Foto: Rafael Nascimento/g1

A cidade do Rio de Janeiro registrou rajadas de vento de quase 60 km/h e chuva fraca em diversos pontos da cidade neste domingo (8). A maior velocidade do vento foi medida na Marambaia, na Zona Oeste, onde as rajadas chegaram a 59,4 km/h . No sábado (7), por conta do temporal, 1 mulher morreu na Zona Oeste do Rio (mais detalhes abaixo) .

Segundo o Alerta Rio, da prefeitura, Aeródromo de Campo dos Afonsos, também na Zona Oeste, os ventos chegaram a 55,5 km/h. Houve ainda registros de ventania de 47,5 km/h no Forte de Copacabana e 44,8 km/h em Guaratiba.

Além dos ventos fortes, o Sistema Alerta Rio registrou chuva fraca em diferentes regiões da cidade na última hora . O maior acumulado foi na Grota Funda, com 3 milímetros, seguido de Madureira, com 2,2 mm, Tijuca, com 1,8 mm, e Irajá, com 1,6 mm.

De acordo com a Climatempo, a previsão para este domingo é de tempo chuvoso durante o dia e à noite, com máxima de 25°C e mínima de 19°C . Previsão do tempo hoje para o Rio de Janeiro: tempo chuvoso durante o dia e à noite.

Bombeiros atendem mais de 140 ocorrências no estado

Desde o início de sábado (7) até o final da manhã deste domingo, a Defesa Civil estadual e o Corpo de Bombeiros foram acionados para atender a 138 ocorrências.

Entre os registros, estão pelo menos 48 salvamentos de pessoas e 13 ocorrências de deslizamento ou desabamento . Um dos casos de desabamento aconteceu em Guaratiba, na Zona Oeste do Rio, deixando 1 mulher morta e outra ferida.

Por conta da chuva no sábado, 1 mulher morreu e uma segunda se feriu — Foto: Divulgação / CBMERJ

A vítima de 68 anos foi resgatada com vida e encaminhada ao Hospital Municipal Pedro II, em Santa Cruz. A outra mulher, identificada como Evelyn Bulgarelli Freitas, de 44 anos, foi encontrada morta sob os escombros.

Duas jovens que estavam desaparecidas no Monte dos Sete Castiçais, em Mesquita, na Baixada Fluminense, foram localizadas e resgatadas na tarde deste domingo (8). Elas estavam no local quando foram surpreendidas pelo temporal de sábado.

O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado por volta das 19h40 e passou a noite fazendo buscas. Militares do quartel de Belford Roxo, com apoio de equipes de Magé e Nilópolis, conseguiram chegar até as vítimas com a ajuda da localização por GPS do celular de uma delas.

Em Nova Iguaçu, 5 pessoas deram entrada no Hospital Geral de Nova Iguaçu (HGNI) após ocorrências relacionadas ao temporal. Quatro receberam alta, enquanto uma permanece internada no CTI, em estado grave, após cair de um andaime.

Com as rajadas, a orientação é evitar se abrigar debaixo de árvores ou coberturas metálicas e não passar próximo a cabos elétricos, outdoors, andaimes e escadas.

A recomendação também é evitar atividades esportivas ao ar livre, principalmente no mar.

Dentro de casa, a recomendação é manter janelas, basculantes e portas de armários fechados . Persianas e cortinas também devem permanecer fechadas para reduzir o risco de espalhamento de estilhaços caso algum vidro se quebre.

articles.title: Adolescente é atingida por árvore durante temporal no interior de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Adolescente de Santa Bárbara d'Oeste foi levada para Pronto-socorro e depois transferida para hospital em Sumaré.
articles.summary: Adolescente atingida por árvore em Santa Bárbara d'Oeste foi transferida para o Hospital Estadual de Sumaré após temporal causar estragos e falta de energia na região.
articles.body:
Uma adolescente de 14 anos ficou gravemente ferida após ser atingida por uma árvore que caiu durante o temporal da tarde de sábado (7) em Santa Bárbara d'Oeste (SP).

A prefeitura informou que a jovem deu entrada em estado grave no Pronto-Socorro Dr. Edison Mano. "Segundo os familiares, a adolescente teria sido atingida pela queda de uma árvore, durante o temporal", comunicou a administração municipal.

"Devido a gravidade do caso, após ser estabilizada, a paciente foi transferida, com o suporte e equipe da UTI móvel do Município, para o Hospital Estadual de Sumaré", completou a prefeitura.

Queda de árvore no Parque dos Ipês, em Santa Bárbara d'Oeste — Foto: Mariane Rosa

Em nota, a Secretaria de Saúde de Santa Bárbara d'Oeste afirmou que a queda de energia durante a chuva não prejudicou o atendimento do PS Edison Mano. Segundo a pasta, o local possui geradores.

Árvore caiu na Praça Coronel Luiz Alves durante o temporal que atingiu Santa Bárbara d'Oeste (SP) na tarde deste sábado (7) — Foto: Tonny Machado

O temporal provocou a queda de árvores, entre elas uma sobre um carro no Jardim Paulista.

Um morador da região central registra o momento que a cobertura de parte da garagem é levada pela força dos ventos. "Furacão, mãe", chega a gritar - assista acima .

A tempestade, que era prevista pela Defesa Civil de São Paulo, também provocou estragos em outros pontos da cidade.

Houve queda de árvore na praça Coronel Luiz Alves, na região central, assim como o destelhamento de parte de um imóvel.

Segundo a Prefeitura de Santa Bárbara d'Oeste, equipes foram mobilizadas para atendimento das ocorrências e a Guarda Municipal atuou para auxiliar no monitoramento de trânsito em áreas afetadas pelas quedas de árvores.

Por conta do temporal, vários imóveis ficaram sem energia elétrica na cidade. Em nota, a CPFL Paulista informou que os problemas foram causados principalmente pela queda de árvores de grande porte e objetos arremessados pelo vento sobre a fiação.

"Em alguns trechos, os danos foram extensos e será necessário reconstruir estruturas que foram destruídas. Todas as equipes foram rapidamente mobilizadas e estão atuando para restabelecer a energia aos clientes afetados, em segurança, no menor tempo possível", informou a empresa.

Além de Santa Bárbara, houve registro de chuva forte em Piracicaba. Segundo a Defesa Civil do Estado, foram registradas rajadas de vento de até 96,1 km/h às 16h.

Moradores fizeram registros da força do vento nos bairros Dois Córregos, Jardim Petrópolis e Santa Cecília.

Em nota, a prefeitura informou que equipes de todas as secretarias municipais estão mobilizadas, juntamente com o Corpo de Bombeiros e a CPFL, para atender chamados como quedas de árvores, interrupções no fornecimento de energia e outras situações provocadas pelas chuvas.
